books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.text: A color lithograph published in 1870, titled “The Fifteenth Amendment. Celebrated May 19th, 1870.” At the center, a parade fills a city street with marching soldiers, a band, and a carriage. Around the border are small scenes: a classroom full of Black children with their teacher, a wedding, a Black man casting a ballot, and Black men in formal dress. Portraits in oval frames around the border include President Ulysses S. Grant, Vice President Schuyler Colfax, and Abraham Lincoln.
stimulus.source_note: Thomas Kelly, publisher, “The Fifteenth Amendment. Celebrated May 19th, 1870,” lithograph after a design by James C. Beard, 1870 (Library of Congress, LCCN2003690776). Public domain. Image viewed before writing; scenes and portraits described from the image itself.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The scenes around the border, including a Black man casting a ballot, celebrate

options.text: the end of the Civil War in 1865.
options.misconception: Background: the war had ended five years earlier, in 1865.

options.text: the impeachment trial of Andrew Johnson in the Senate.
options.misconception: Background: Johnson’s trial was in 1868, and no one printed a celebration of it.

options.text: the founding of the Freedmen’s Bureau.
options.misconception: Background: the Bureau was founded in 1865, and the print is dated 1870.

options.text: Black men's right to vote under the Fifteenth Amendment.

rationales.A: Background: the war had ended five years earlier, in 1865.
rationales.B: Background: Johnson’s trial was in 1868, and no one printed a celebration of it.
rationales.C: Background: the Bureau was founded in 1865, and the print is dated 1870.
rationales.D: The border scenes show a Black man casting a ballot, a classroom, and a wedding — the rights of citizenship the Fifteenth Amendment secured by barring denial of the vote on account of race.
rationales.general:
1. The border scenes show a classroom, a wedding, and a Black man casting a ballot.
2. Those are the rights of citizenship — schooling, family, and the vote.
3. Background: the Fifteenth Amendment, ratified in 1870, said the vote could not be denied on account of race.
4. The print is a victory poster for that new right.
Remember: the scenes around the border show the rights the amendment secured.
